cards.statement: An engineer selects file search for managed chunking of product manuals uploaded to a Foundry agent.
cards.explanation: File search chunks uploaded files during managed ingestion, reducing the document-preparation code the developer maintains.

source.title: File search tool for agents

cards.statement: Grounding with Bing Search can give application developers raw search-tool output for their own processing.
cards.explanation: Foundry Agent Service returns model-generated answers from Bing grounding, rather than exposing the raw search-tool output.
cards.misconception: Bing grounding exposes raw search results to the application.

source.title: Use Grounding with Bing Search tools

cards.statement: A Foundry agent's Code Interpreter sandbox runs in the same Azure region as the agent's Foundry project.
cards.explanation: Code Interpreter runs in Azure Container Apps dynamic sessions placed in the Foundry project's own region, which matters when an engineer plans for data residency.

source.title: Use Code Interpreter with Microsoft Foundry agents

cards.statement: An Azure AI Search vectorizer generates document embeddings during an indexer's ingestion pipeline.
cards.explanation: An Azure AI Search vectorizer converts query input to vectors at query time. Indexing uses embedding skills.
cards.misconception: A vectorizer performs the embedding skill's indexing job.

source.title: Integrated vector embedding in Azure AI Search

cards.statement: For schema-shaped metadata from videos, an engineer selects Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools.
cards.explanation: Content Understanding lets an engineer configure video analyzers to return custom fields from visual and audio evidence.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: Content Understanding video overview

cards.statement: An engineer selects Phi-4-mini-instruct as a small language model for captioning product photos.
cards.explanation: Phi-4-mini-instruct accepts text input only. Phi-4-multimodal-instruct is the Phi-4 option that accepts text, images and audio.
cards.misconception: Every small Phi-4 chat model can read image input.

source.title: Foundry Models from partners and community

cards.statement: An engineer chooses fine-tuning to keep a Foundry app grounded in inventory records that change throughout the day.
cards.explanation: RAG retrieves changing records for grounding. Fine-tuning targets model behavior or task performance rather than adding fresh knowledge.
cards.misconception: Fine-tuning is the retrieval method for frequently changing facts.

source.title: Retrieval augmented generation and indexes

cards.statement: An engineer selects an Azure AI Search indexer to ingest Azure Blob Storage files on a recurring schedule.
cards.explanation: An indexer pulls from a supported data source and refreshes the target index on a configured schedule.

source.title: Indexer overview

cards.statement: For a Chat Completions coding app, an engineer selects a gpt-5.1-codex deployment in Azure OpenAI.
cards.explanation: gpt-5.1-codex uses the Responses API. A Chat Completions app needs a compatible model or an API migration.
cards.misconception: A coding model supports the application's existing Chat Completions API.
cards.volatilityNote: Model-specific API support and model availability can change.

source.title: Foundry Models sold by Azure

cards.statement: For Global Standard, Azure stores model data at rest in the designated Azure geography.
cards.explanation: Global Standard keeps stored data in its designated geography; its deployment type governs inference processing separately.

source.title: Understanding deployment types

cards.statement: With Data Zone Standard, Azure confines inference processing to the Foundry resource's Azure region.
cards.explanation: Data Zone Standard routes inference within the specified Microsoft data zone, which can include multiple Azure regions.
cards.misconception: A data zone deployment pins inference to one region.

source.title: Understanding deployment types

cards.statement: Microsoft suggests Global Provisioned when a region lacks PTU capacity and global data processing is acceptable.
cards.explanation: Global Provisioned reserves PTUs but may process data in any Azure region, so Microsoft offers it as a fix for missing regional PTU capacity when no geography rule requires local processing.

source.title: Understanding deployment types in Microsoft Foundry Models

cards.statement: An Azure OpenAI v1 caller requires a monthly api-version value when submitting a Responses request.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI v1 removes the requirement for a dated api-version query parameter in GA requests.
cards.misconception: Azure OpenAI v1 keeps the dated API-version requirement.

source.title: Azure OpenAI v1 API

cards.statement: An Azure OpenAI v1 developer sets OpenAI() base_url to the resource endpoint ending in /openai/v1/.
cards.explanation: The OpenAI Python client targets Azure OpenAI v1 through base_url, including the /openai/v1/ route.

source.title: Azure OpenAI v1 API

cards.statement: An app puts the catalog model name in the model parameter to call a deployment that has a custom name.
cards.explanation: During inference, the model parameter carries the deployment name. A deployment given a custom name at creation is called by that name, not by the catalog model name.
cards.misconception: The catalog model name routes to a deployment whatever the deployment is named.

source.title: Deploy Microsoft Foundry Models in the Foundry portal

cards.statement: With azure-ai-projects 2.3.0, a developer sends embeddings.create requests through the project endpoint.
cards.explanation: Embedding requests go to the direct Azure OpenAI model endpoint. The Foundry project endpoint currently does not route embeddings.
cards.misconception: The Foundry project endpoint exposes embedding inference.
cards.volatilityNote: The project endpoint's supported inference routes can expand in later service or SDK releases.

source.title: Microsoft Foundry SDKs and endpoints

cards.statement: In Foundry Agents v2, a developer who saves edited instructions for an agent creates a new agent version.
cards.explanation: Saved Foundry agent versions are immutable, so any change is saved as a new version. Code refers to an agent as <agent_name>:<version>.

source.title: Agent development lifecycle in Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: Foundry migrates existing connection secrets when an engineer attaches their own Azure Key Vault.
cards.explanation: Foundry does not migrate connection secrets into a newly attached Azure Key Vault. The engineer recreates the connections afterward.
cards.misconception: Attaching a customer-managed vault migrates connection secrets.
cards.volatilityNote: Support for migrating existing secrets to a customer-managed vault can change.

source.title: Add a new connection to your project

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI can create separate quota pools per resource for the same subscription, region, model, and deployment type.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI shares quota across resources for the same subscription, region, model, and deployment type. Deployment allocations draw from that shared pool.
cards.misconception: Creating another Azure OpenAI resource creates an independent quota pool.

source.title: Manage Azure OpenAI quota

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI TPM enforcement uses the token count that Azure Monitor reports for billing.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI enforces TPM using a request-time estimate of potential token processing. Azure Monitor reports billed consumption after successful processing.
cards.misconception: Rate enforcement and billing use the same token count.

source.title: Manage Azure OpenAI quota

cards.statement: Azure Monitor splits Azure OpenAI's blocked-request metric by the content category behind each block.
cards.explanation: The Blocked Volume metric counts Azure OpenAI requests rejected by content filters. Its Category dimension helps an engineer identify the categories causing rejections.

source.title: Monitoring data reference for Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: Azure AI Search's top-level running status confirms that an indexer is executing its latest run.
cards.explanation: Azure AI Search's top-level running status means the indexer is ready to execute. The execution result's status shows whether a particular run is active.
cards.misconception: An indexer's top-level status describes its current execution.

source.title: Monitor indexer status and results

cards.statement: An Azure AI Search indexer run can report success while some documents in that run failed to index.
cards.explanation: A run still counts as successful while its document errors stay below the indexer's Max failed items setting, so an engineer checks a run's errors even after success.

source.title: Monitor indexer status and results

cards.statement: An administrator assigns Foundry User to a project's managed identity for Foundry resource access.
cards.explanation: Microsoft Foundry checks the project's managed identity as a separate caller. Foundry User on the Foundry resource authorizes that identity's project operations.

source.title: Role-based access control for Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: Foundry User on a Foundry resource gives a developer permission to publish agents from its projects.
cards.explanation: Foundry User covers building and testing agents in a project. Publishing agents needs at least Foundry Project Manager at the Foundry resource scope.
cards.misconception: The developer role for building agents also covers publishing them.

source.title: Role-based access control for Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI's Time to Response metric includes network latency between the client app and the API endpoint.
cards.explanation: Time to Response is measured at the API gateway up to the first response, so client-side network latency is outside it. End-to-end timing comes from the app's own logging.
cards.misconception: Service-side latency metrics capture the client's full round trip.

source.title: Monitoring data reference for Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: Foundry clients keep the same endpoint hostname when DNS routes requests through a private endpoint.
cards.explanation: Foundry clients retain their resource endpoint connection string for private access. DNS resolves that hostname to the private endpoint's IP address inside the connected virtual network.

source.title: Configure network isolation for Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 can return HTTP 400 with content_filter when the Responses API blocks a prompt.
cards.explanation: A blocked Azure OpenAI v1 Responses input raises BadRequestError in Python. The content_filter code identifies a guardrail rejection for the app to handle.

source.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API

cards.statement: A developer changes a Foundry model's default guardrail by editing its built-in policy.
cards.explanation: Microsoft's built-in default guardrail is read-only. A developer creates a custom guardrail and assigns it to the model deployment to change the safety policy.
cards.misconception: The built-in default policy is editable.

source.title: Configure guardrails and controls in Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: In a Foundry guardrail annotation, a user prompt attack with detected set to true means the request was blocked.
cards.explanation: detected only reports that Prompt Shields flagged an attack. The filtered value shows whether the guardrail blocked it; in annotate mode an attack is detected but not filtered.
cards.misconception: Detection of an attack implies the guardrail blocked it.

source.title: Prompt Shields in Azure AI Content Safety

cards.statement: Prompt Shields treats a user's request to reply only in URL encoding as a user prompt attack.
cards.explanation: Encoding attacks are a user prompt attack subtype: ciphers and character transformations can slip past system rules, so requests for encoded output get flagged.

source.title: Prompt Shields in Azure AI Content Safety

cards.statement: A Foundry guardrail's protected material code annotation can cite a public GitHub repository for matched code.
cards.explanation: When protected material code is detected, the annotation can carry an example GitHub repository URL and its license. Microsoft strongly recommends showing that citation with the code.

source.title: How to configure guardrails and controls in Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: Foundry content safety evaluators use the developer's model deployment to score harmful response content.
cards.explanation: Foundry content safety evaluators use Microsoft's hosted safety models. Developers supply Foundry project information rather than a judge deployment_name.
cards.misconception: Safety evaluators use the application's model deployment as their judge.

source.title: Risk and safety evaluators

cards.statement: Foundry safety evaluation results include a reason explaining the assigned harm severity.
cards.explanation: Foundry content safety evaluators return a severity score and an explanatory reason. The reason helps a developer understand the assigned score.

source.title: Risk and safety evaluators

cards.statement: The Dataset evaluation target in Microsoft Foundry reruns the agent to produce responses.
cards.explanation: Foundry's Dataset evaluation scores responses already stored in the dataset. A developer selects this target to assess captured outputs.
cards.misconception: Evaluating saved responses reruns the original agent.

source.title: Run evaluations from the Microsoft Foundry portal

cards.statement: Foundry prompt-agent tracing can capture tool-call arguments when project tracing is enabled.
cards.explanation: Tool arguments can enter Foundry prompt-agent trace telemetry. Developers redact secrets and personal data before those values enter telemetry.

source.title: Set up tracing in Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 apps can continue a Responses API chat by resending earlier output items as input.
cards.explanation: Besides previous_response_id chaining, an app can append the earlier response's output items to its next input, keeping conversation state in its own code.

source.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API

cards.statement: With azure-ai-projects 2.3.0, an app runs Foundry evaluations through the client from get_openai_client().
cards.explanation: AIProjectClient handles project setup such as connections. The OpenAI-compatible client from get_openai_client() runs Responses calls, agents and evaluations.

source.title: Get started with Microsoft Foundry SDKs and endpoints

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 JSON mode validates generated fields against the schema described in the prompt.
cards.explanation: JSON mode targets valid JSON rather than conformity to a schema requested in the prompt. Azure OpenAI structured outputs provide schema enforcement.
cards.misconception: Requesting a schema in the prompt makes JSON mode enforce that schema.

source.title: How to use JSON mode with Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: A Microsoft Foundry developer maps context as a plain string when running Groundedness evaluation.
cards.explanation: Join retrieved chunks into one string before mapping them to context. The Groundedness evaluator uses this supplied source material to assess the response.

source.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) evaluators

cards.statement: Microsoft Foundry Relevance evaluation uses a reference answer as its scoring comparison.
cards.explanation: The Relevance evaluator compares a response with the user's query. Its data mapping uses query and response to judge how well the response addresses that request.
cards.misconception: Relevance evaluates responses by comparing them with a reference answer.

source.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) evaluators

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 Global Batch accepts requests for different model deployments within one submitted job.
cards.explanation: A Global Batch job targets one model deployment. Submit separate files and jobs when requests target different deployments.
cards.misconception: A batch file can mix requests for different model deployments.

source.title: Getting started with Azure OpenAI batch deployments

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 Batch API returns completed responses in the same order as the submitted input lines.
cards.explanation: Match Azure OpenAI Batch API outputs to their input requests by custom_id. Output line position does not reliably identify the corresponding input line.
cards.misconception: Batch output positions correspond to input positions, so an application can zip the files together.

source.title: Getting started with Azure OpenAI batch deployments

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 structured outputs keep nullable properties in the schema's required list.
cards.explanation: A nullable property still appears as a key in structured output. Declare it required and include null in its type to represent an optional value.

source.title: How to use structured outputs with Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 structured outputs reject schemas with recursive references to their own definitions.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI structured outputs support recursive schemas through JSON Schema references. A schema can refer back to its root or to a definition that references itself.
cards.misconception: Azure OpenAI's supported JSON Schema subset excludes recursive references.

source.title: How to use structured outputs with Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: Foundry Agent Service can automatically execute an app's local Python function for a v2 prompt agent.
cards.explanation: Application code executes a requested custom function and returns its result. Foundry Agent Service receives the result to continue the prompt agent's response.
cards.misconception: A service-side prompt agent executes the application's local function body.

source.title: Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents

cards.statement: A Foundry Agents v2 conversation keeps its stored items when the model truncates input past its context size.
cards.explanation: When a conversation outgrows the model's context window, only the input sent to the model is truncated. The conversation object keeps every item for later turns.

source.title: Build with runtime components in Foundry Agent Service

cards.statement: If a Foundry toolbox file search tool omits vector_store_ids, its callers pass the store IDs in tools/call.
cards.explanation: Pinned vector_store_ids fix the store for every call. Leaving them out at toolbox creation makes callers pass store IDs in tools/call arguments, so a multitenant app searches per request.

source.title: File search tool for Microsoft Foundry agents

cards.statement: A Foundry Agents v2 app treats its Files API upload response as confirmation that file search ingestion has finished.
cards.explanation: File upload and vector-store ingestion have separate completion states. Wait for ingestion to complete successfully before querying the new file.
cards.misconception: A successful upload means the file is ready for retrieval.

source.title: File search tool for Microsoft Foundry agents

cards.statement: Code Interpreter can fetch a public web page during execution in a Foundry Agents v2 sandbox.
cards.explanation: The Microsoft-managed Code Interpreter sandbox blocks outbound network requests. An app supplies needed data through another approved integration.
cards.misconception: The managed Code Interpreter sandbox has outbound internet access.

source.title: Use Code Interpreter with Microsoft Foundry agents

cards.statement: A Microsoft Agent Framework app can use a Foundry toolbox's tools through its MCP-compatible endpoint.
cards.explanation: Toolboxes are Foundry-homed but not Foundry-bound: any MCP-compatible runtime or client, including Microsoft Agent Framework and LangGraph, can use one.

source.title: What is Toolbox in Microsoft Foundry?

cards.statement: By default, SequentialBuilder passes prior input and response messages to the next agent in a Python workflow.
cards.explanation: Microsoft Agent Framework's SequentialBuilder forwards the preceding agent's full conversation. This gives the next agent both incoming context and generated responses.
cards.volatilityNote: SDK releases can change the default message propagation of SequentialBuilder.

source.title: Microsoft Agent Framework sequential orchestration

cards.statement: A Foundry Agents v2 app copies a function call's call_id into function_call_output when returning results.
cards.explanation: The function_call_output call_id matches the originating function call. That identifier associates the submitted result with the requested operation.

source.title: Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents

cards.statement: A Foundry Agents v2 app uses response.id as approval_request_id when approving an MCP tool call.
cards.explanation: approval_request_id matches the mcp_approval_request item's id. This associates the approval decision with the requested tool operation.
cards.misconception: The enclosing response ID identifies the tool's approval request.

source.title: Connect agents to MCP server endpoints

cards.statement: For gpt-5.6-sol in Azure OpenAI v1, text.verbosity controls the effort spent on reasoning.
cards.explanation: gpt-5.6-sol uses text.verbosity for visible answer detail. The setting changes conciseness, not reasoning effort.
cards.misconception: The requested answer detail determines how much reasoning the model performs.
cards.volatilityNote: Model-specific parameter support can change in later deployment versions.

source.title: Azure OpenAI reasoning models

cards.statement: A gpt-5.6-sol app reads earlier turns' reasoning text from items kept with reasoning.context set to all_turns.
cards.explanation: all_turns lets the model reuse earlier reasoning items, but the items stay opaque and the API never returns their text. The reasoning summary parameter gives an app a summary instead.
cards.misconception: Persisted reasoning items expose their reasoning text to the app.

source.title: Azure OpenAI reasoning models

cards.statement: For gpt-5.6-sol, Azure OpenAI v1 Responses API reserves reasoning tokens outside max_output_tokens.
cards.explanation: For gpt-5.6-sol, max_output_tokens covers reasoning and visible output together. Reasoning consumes part of that generation budget.
cards.misconception: Reasoning tokens use a separate budget beyond the output-token cap.
cards.volatilityNote: New model versions can change how output-token limits account for reasoning.

source.title: Azure OpenAI reasoning models

cards.statement: To combine reasoning with function tools, a gpt-5.6-sol app uses Azure OpenAI v1's Responses API.
cards.explanation: gpt-5.6-sol combines reasoning and function tools through the Responses API. Chat Completions tool calls require reasoning_effort set to none.
cards.volatilityNote: Tool and reasoning compatibility varies with the deployed model and API family.

source.title: Work with chat completion models

cards.statement: An Azure OpenAI v1 app puts reusable prompt content before changing user input to improve cache reuse.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI matches cached prompt prefixes. Keeping the shared prefix identical lets repeated requests reuse earlier input processing.

source.title: Prompt caching

cards.statement: A Microsoft Foundry prompt-agent trace records model calls and tool executions as separately timed spans.
cards.explanation: A prompt-agent trace separates model operations from tool operations. Inspecting their spans helps an engineer locate the step responsible for a latency spike.

source.title: Agent tracing overview

cards.statement: Microsoft Foundry keeps prompt-agent traces in its own project store until an engineer connects Application Insights.
cards.explanation: Foundry tracing is off by default: no trace data is collected until the project is connected to Azure Monitor Application Insights, which then stores the traces.
cards.misconception: Foundry collects traces before any telemetry resource is connected.

source.title: Microsoft Foundry tracing and data handling

cards.statement: A GroupChatBuilder app reads the conversation in termination_condition to stop writer-reviewer rounds.
cards.explanation: GroupChatBuilder passes conversation messages to termination_condition. The application checks review history and returns a Boolean decision to end or continue the loop.

source.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Workflows Orchestrations - Group Chat

cards.statement: An outgoing AgentExecutor edge condition receives the generated response text as a string.
cards.explanation: An AgentExecutor sends an AgentExecutorResponse to its outgoing edge condition. Routing code reads message.agent_response.text when it needs the generated text.
cards.misconception: A conditional routing callback receives the agent's plain response text instead of its response object.

source.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Workflows - Edges

cards.statement: The app sends a product photo and a logo as two input images in one GPT-Image-2 edit call.
cards.explanation: The Image Edit API accepts several input images per request, up to 16 on Azure OpenAI, so the app can combine a product shot with a logo.

source.title: Azure OpenAI image generation models

cards.statement: The app can request a hosted image URL as the output from GPT-Image-2.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2 returns base64 image data that the app decodes.
cards.misconception: GPT-Image-2 returns hosted URLs.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

source.title: Azure OpenAI image generation models

cards.statement: GPT-Image-2 returns PNG when the app leaves output_format out of its request.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI image generation defaults output_format to PNG, so the app receives PNG unless it requests another supported format.

source.title: Azure OpenAI image generation models

cards.statement: GPT-Image-2's output_compression setting controls PNG compression for the app's generated images.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2's output_compression setting applies to JPEG output.
cards.misconception: PNG supports output_compression.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

source.title: Azure OpenAI image generation models

cards.statement: The app can request several output images from GPT-Image-2 in one generation call.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2's n parameter requests separate output images.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

source.title: Azure OpenAI image generation models

cards.statement: The app can mark an edit target using opaque pixels in a GPT-Image-2 image mask.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2 inpainting targets areas marked by transparent mask pixels.
cards.misconception: Opaque mask pixels mark edits.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

source.title: Transparency note for Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: GPT-Image-2's Image Edit API rejects a JPEG image because of its input format.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2's Image Edit API accepts JPEG input files.
cards.misconception: Editing requires PNG input.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

source.title: Azure OpenAI image generation models

cards.statement: An app's GPT-Image-2 edit mask must be a PNG file with the same dimensions as the input image.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI requires an image edit mask to be a PNG file with the same dimensions as the input image it accompanies.

source.title: Azure OpenAI image generation models

cards.statement: GPT-Image-2 limits the app's size parameter to the 1024x1024, 1024x1536 and 1536x1024 values.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2 accepts custom WIDTHxHEIGHT sizes when both edges are multiples of 16 px and the aspect ratio stays between 1:3 and 3:1. The three fixed sizes belong to GPT-Image-1 models.
cards.misconception: GPT-Image-2 keeps GPT-Image-1's fixed size list.

source.title: Azure OpenAI image generation models

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 apps pair input_text and input_image in one Responses API message.
cards.explanation: A Responses API message carries the question text and the image as separate content parts, so the model reads both in one request.

source.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 apps can set image_url to a bare base64 string for Responses API image input.
cards.explanation: An inline Responses API image uses a data URI containing the MIME type and base64 payload.
cards.misconception: Bare base64 fits image_url.

source.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 apps can compare several images in one Responses API request to a vision-capable model.
cards.explanation: A vision-capable Azure OpenAI deployment receives the supplied images together for comparison.

source.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 apps use detail=high on input_image to increase the Responses API's output-token limit.
cards.explanation: Responses API detail controls image processing fidelity, rather than output-token limits.
cards.misconception: Image detail controls answer length.

source.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API

cards.statement: A Content Understanding 2025-11-01 video analyzer with enableSegment splits by the contentCategories description.
cards.explanation: The contentCategories description acts as a prompt that guides segment boundaries, so segments follow the logic the app describes. A video analyzer takes one category.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: What is a Content Understanding analyzer? Configuration and reference

cards.statement: Content Understanding 2025-11-01 video transcription labels sound effects as events in the transcript.
cards.explanation: Content Understanding transcribes spoken words. Its video analysis excludes detection of non-speech audio signals such as sound effects.
cards.misconception: Video transcription labels non-speech events.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools
cards.volatilityNote: Later service models can expand the audio events supported by video analysis.

source.title: Transparency note: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

cards.statement: Content Understanding 2025-11-01 places video schema fields in content objects for the generated segments.
cards.explanation: A segmented video result places extracted fields in the content objects for its segments. The segments array contains boundary and category metadata.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: AudioVisual analysis: extracting structured content with Azure Content Understanding

cards.statement: Microsoft recommends Content Understanding 2025-11-01 image analyzers for text-first extraction from receipt photos.
cards.explanation: For image analysis driven primarily by extracted text, Microsoft recommends a document field extraction schema.
cards.misconception: An image file calls for an image analyzer even when text drives the analysis.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools image solutions

cards.statement: An app reads shot-change timestamps from cameraShotTimesMs with returnDetails=true.
cards.explanation: cameraShotTimesMs marks camera-shot changes, rather than sampled key frames. Enable returnDetails to include those video timestamps.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: Content Analyzers - Get Result

cards.statement: A Python Azure AI Content Safety SDK app passes raw image bytes into ImageData's content argument.
cards.explanation: The Azure AI Content Safety Python SDK accepts file.read() bytes in ImageData(content=...). The SDK prepares that image data for the service request.

source.title: Quickstart: Analyze image content

cards.statement: Azure AI Content Safety 2024-09-01 can accept a brand's logo-usage rule in image:analyze's categories array.
cards.explanation: image:analyze accepts predefined harm categories: Hate, SelfHarm, Sexual and Violence. Its categories array selects checks rather than defining a brand policy.
cards.misconception: The categories array defines application-specific visual policy rules.

source.title: Image Operations - Analyze Image

cards.statement: Azure AI Content Safety 2024-09-01 can rate one image at nonzero severity in both Sexual and Violence.
cards.explanation: Image moderation classification is multi-label: one analyzed image can score as both sexual and violent content in the same call.

source.title: Quickstart: Analyze image content

cards.statement: Azure AI Content Safety 2024-09-01 uses content for image input when the app also supplies blobUrl.
cards.explanation: Azure AI Content Safety refuses an image request that supplies both content and blobUrl. The app chooses one image input representation.
cards.misconception: The API resolves conflicting image inputs by preferring content.

source.title: Image Operations - Analyze Image

cards.statement: Azure AI Content Safety image:analyze returns an Accepted/Rejected verdict for the app's image.
cards.explanation: image:analyze returns category severity scores. The application compares them with its policy thresholds to decide whether to display the image.
cards.misconception: The standalone image API applies the app's accept/reject policy.

source.title: Image Operations - Analyze Image

cards.statement: To screen text embedded in an image with Prompt Shields 2024-09-01, an app first extracts that text as strings.
cards.explanation: text:shieldPrompt takes a userPrompt string and a documents array of strings and has no image field, so text inside an image is extracted before the call.

source.title: Quickstart: Detect prompt attacks with Prompt Shields

cards.statement: A GPT-Image-2 app can check attached Content Credentials for tampering with the image's generation metadata.
cards.explanation: Content Credentials attach cryptographically signed provenance metadata. A verifier checks whether that metadata has changed since signing.
cards.volatilityNote: Model-specific provenance support and metadata formats can evolve.

source.title: Content provenance

cards.statement: An app proves who prompted GPT-Image-2 by validating Microsoft Foundry's attached Content Credentials.
cards.explanation: Microsoft Foundry provenance may identify a model or service while omitting the person who prompted it. A recipient needs separate attribution records.
cards.misconception: Authentic generation metadata proves the prompting user's identity.

source.title: Content provenance

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI checks submitted image-generation prompts for protected art and studio characters.
cards.explanation: The Azure OpenAI protected-material policy targets image prompts that request covered art or studio characters.

source.title: Default safety policies in Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: A translation app receives per-language detection results for a mixed document from Azure Language in Foundry Tools.
cards.explanation: Azure Language returns one predominant language per document. A translation app splits multilingual content into separate documents when it needs separate source-language results.
cards.misconception: A multilingual document receives a detection result for its constituent languages.

source.title: How to use language detection

cards.statement: An Azure Translator Text API 2026-06-06 app selects LLM translation to apply the tone parameter.
cards.explanation: Translator Text API 2026-06-06 accepts tone controls for LLM-based translation. The app requests LLM translation and supplies its desired tone for the target text.
cards.volatilityNote: Later API versions can change which translation models accept tone controls.

source.title: Migrate to Translator Text API 2026-06-06

cards.statement: A PII 2026-05-01 caller reads masked entity values from the response's entities[].text field.
cards.explanation: Azure Language PII returns the detected source value in entities[].text. The redactedText field contains the document with the selected redaction policy applied.
cards.misconception: PII redaction also masks the source text recorded in the entity list.

source.title: Analyze Text - Analyze Text

cards.statement: An app using Azure Translator Text API v3.0 omits from to select source-language detection.
cards.explanation: Translator Text API v3.0 detects the input language when from is omitted. This suits plain-text requests whose source language the app does not already know.

source.title: Translator Translate Method

cards.statement: An Azure Translator Text API v3.0 app uses category as a prompt for its preferred writing style.
cards.explanation: Translator Text API v3.0 category identifies a deployed Custom Translator system. Supply that system's Category ID rather than a free-form writing-style instruction.
cards.misconception: The category parameter accepts a natural-language instruction describing the desired translation style.

source.title: Translator Translate Method

cards.statement: An app repeats to in an Azure Translator Text API v3.0 request to translate text into several target languages.
cards.explanation: Translator Text API v3.0 accepts repeated to query parameters. Its response contains a translation for the requested target languages.

source.title: Translator Translate Method

cards.statement: An Azure Language NER request with GPE in inclusionList also returns Location entities tagged Structural.
cards.explanation: Prebuilt NER filters by type or by tag: GPE in inclusionList returns only geopolitical Location entities, so Location entities tagged Structural or Geological drop out.
cards.misconception: Including a tag in inclusionList returns its whole parent entity type.

source.title: How to perform Named Entity Recognition (NER)

cards.statement: An Azure OpenAI v1 app can use a nested anyOf under an object root to extract either of two entity shapes.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI structured outputs accept supported anyOf schemas below the root. Wrap alternate entity shapes in an object property because the root cannot be anyOf.

source.title: How to use structured outputs with Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 returns a safety refusal inside the JSON object requested by an entity-extraction app.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI exposes a refusal separately from the parsed structured result. An extraction app checks for a refusal before reading the requested entity data.
cards.misconception: A safety refusal follows the application's structured-output schema.

source.title: How to use structured outputs with Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: A Python Speech SDK SpeechRecognizer built from speech_config alone listens to the device microphone.
cards.explanation: Creating SpeechRecognizer with speech_config and no AudioConfig makes the Python Speech SDK capture the device microphone. AudioConfig(filename=...) switches input to a file.

source.title: How to recognize speech

cards.statement: The Python Speech SDK sends finalized transcription text through the recognizing event.
cards.explanation: The recognizing event carries intermediate recognition results that can change as more audio arrives. An app uses recognized events for final recognition results.
cards.misconception: The recognizing event delivers completed transcriptions suitable for final-result handling.

source.title: How to recognize speech

cards.statement: A Python Speech SDK app reads German translation text through the result's translations['de'] entry.
cards.explanation: Speech SDK translation results map target-language codes to translated text in translations. The 'de' entry contains the German translation.

source.title: How to translate speech

cards.statement: A Python Speech SDK app reads synthesis bytes from result.audio_data with audio_config=None.
cards.explanation: audio_config=None keeps synthesis output in memory. The result's audio_data contains a bytes object that the app can forward to another service.

source.title: How to synthesize speech from text

cards.statement: A Python Speech SDK app sets SpeechConfig.endpoint_id to use a deployed custom speech model.
cards.explanation: SpeechConfig.endpoint_id selects the deployed custom speech endpoint used by SpeechRecognizer.

source.title: How to recognize speech

cards.statement: The Python Speech SDK favors speech_synthesis_voice_name over a different voice named in the app's SSML.
cards.explanation: For SSML synthesis, the voice element selects the voice and overrides the SpeechConfig voice setting.
cards.misconception: The SDK configuration's voice setting takes precedence over the voice specified in SSML.

source.title: How to synthesize speech from text

cards.statement: In a Speech to text batch transcription request, an app puts a custom speech endpoint URL in model.self.
cards.explanation: Batch transcription takes the custom model's URI, its top-level self value, in model.self. Batch use of a custom speech model needs no hosted deployment endpoint.
cards.misconception: Batch transcription selects a custom speech deployment endpoint instead of a model resource.

source.title: Create a batch transcription

cards.statement: A Realtime app on Azure OpenAI v1 gets user speech transcripts by naming a transcription deployment in session.update.
cards.explanation: User-audio transcription is opt-in: naming a transcription model deployment in input_audio_transcription makes the session emit conversation.item.audio_transcription.completed events.

source.title: Use the GPT Realtime API for speech and audio with Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: For manual turns, Azure OpenAI v1 Realtime starts a model response when the app sends input_audio_buffer.commit.
cards.explanation: For manual Realtime turns, input_audio_buffer.commit adds the user's audio to conversation state. The app sends response.create to request the model's answer.
cards.misconception: Committing audio in manual turn mode also requests a model-generated answer.

source.title: Use the GPT Realtime API for speech and audio with Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: An Azure AI Search app uses search with vectorQueries to merge keyword and vector results in one request.
cards.explanation: Azure AI Search runs the text and vector query paths in parallel, then combines their ranked results using Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

source.title: Hybrid search using vectors and full-text search in Azure AI Search

cards.statement: An Azure AI Search app uses semantic reranking to fetch documents missed by its first retrieval stage.
cards.explanation: Semantic ranker reorders documents supplied by initial retrieval. Increase the initial candidate set when relevant documents are missing.
cards.misconception: Semantic reranking retrieves additional documents that the initial search missed.

source.title: Semantic ranking in Azure AI Search

cards.statement: Azure AI Search writes fresh wording for the app's returned semantic answers using a generative language model.
cards.explanation: Azure AI Search semantic answers extract verbatim passages from indexed documents. The source text needs to contain an answer-like passage.
cards.misconception: Semantic answers generate a new answer from the retrieved content.

source.title: Return a semantic answer in Azure AI Search

cards.statement: An Azure AI Search app maps contentOffset to the Text Merge skill's offsets input to place embedded-image OCR text.
cards.explanation: Text Merge uses image contentOffset values to insert OCR text into the original document body alongside surrounding text.

source.title: Text Merge cognitive skill

cards.statement: Azure AI Search pairs Custom Web API skill outputs with inputs by their positions in the values arrays.
cards.explanation: Azure AI Search correlates custom skill records by recordId. A Web API returns the input recordId with its corresponding enrichment even when response records arrive in a different order.
cards.misconception: The request and response array positions identify the same custom skill record.

source.title: Custom Web API skill in an Azure AI Search enrichment pipeline

cards.statement: Azure AI Search index projections can repeat a parent document's title on its chunk documents.
cards.explanation: Map /document/title in the projection selector alongside the chunk content. Search results then carry the source title on the chunk documents.

source.title: Define an index projection for parent-child indexing

cards.statement: An Azure AI Search app treats equal vector dimensions as sufficient for mixing query and document embedding models.
cards.explanation: Use the same embedding model for document indexing and query vectors in Azure AI Search. Equal dimensions alone do not align the models' representations.
cards.misconception: Matching vector lengths makes different embedding models interchangeable for retrieval.

source.title: Generate embeddings for search queries and documents

cards.statement: An Azure AI Search app favors preFilter over postFilter when a selective vector-query filter causes missing matches.
cards.explanation: preFilter evaluates the filter during HNSW traversal. This avoids the false negatives that shard-level postFilter can introduce for selective filters.

source.title: Add a filter to a vector query in Azure AI Search

cards.statement: An Azure AI Search developer can add a retrievable string field with searchable=false to a semantic configuration.
cards.explanation: Semantic configuration inputs are searchable, retrievable string fields. Set searchable=true on the text field before using it for semantic ranking.
cards.misconception: A retrievable string field is eligible for semantic ranking even when full-text search is disabled.

source.title: Configure semantic ranker and return captions in search results

cards.statement: Custom analyzers based on prebuilt-document in Content Understanding 2025-11-01 run OCR by default.
cards.explanation: A custom analyzer inherits prebuilt-document's defaults, where enableOcr is true, so scanned pages and image-based PDFs yield text without extra configuration.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: What is a Content Understanding analyzer? Configuration and reference

cards.statement: Content Understanding 2025-11-01 requires a customer LLM deployment for an app's prebuilt-layout calls.
cards.explanation: prebuilt-layout performs content and layout extraction without a customer language model or embedding model deployment.
cards.misconception: The layout analyzer depends on a customer-provided LLM deployment.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools
cards.volatilityNote: The model requirements of prebuilt analyzers can evolve as the service changes.

source.title: Prebuilt analyzers in Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

cards.statement: A Content Understanding 2025-11-01 app polls the Operation-Location URL for its asynchronous document result.
cards.explanation: The Analyze POST returns an operation URL. Poll that URL until the result's status is Succeeded before consuming the extracted document fields.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: Quickstart: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

cards.statement: Content Understanding 2025-11-01 keeps an invoice's spelled-out month names in the app's valueDate result.
cards.explanation: A date-typed Content Understanding field returns valueDate in ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DD. The value uses a normalized representation rather than the invoice's original formatting.
cards.misconception: The typed date value preserves the source document formatting.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: Content Analyzers - Get Result

cards.statement: Content Understanding 2025-11-01 sends an unfamiliar document to an implicit other category.
cards.explanation: An app defines an explicit catch-all category for unmatched documents. Otherwise, Content Understanding assigns a category from the app's configured list.
cards.misconception: The classifier creates a fallback category for documents outside the configured categories.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: Content Understanding classification/segmentation

cards.statement: An app locates a PDF field's supporting region from its source string in Content Understanding 2025-11-01.
cards.explanation: A document field's source encodes its page number and spatial coordinates. A review UI uses this data to highlight the supporting PDF region.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: Document Analysis: Extract Structured Content with Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

cards.statement: A custom Content Understanding 2025-11-01 analyzer supplies generated field confidence by default.
cards.explanation: Generated document fields have opt-in confidence scores. Set estimateFieldSourceAndConfidence for the analyzer or estimateSourceAndConfidence for a field.
cards.misconception: Adding generated document fields enables confidence scoring by default.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools document solutions

cards.statement: An app can preserve merged cells with tableFormat:html in Content Understanding 2025-11-01 document output.
cards.explanation: HTML table output preserves complex cell structures. GitHub Flavored Markdown table syntax lacks support for merged cells and rich headers.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: Content Analyzers - Get

cards.statement: An app can fix recurring OCR character errors with labeled samples in Content Understanding 2025-11-01.
cards.explanation: Labeled samples guide document field extraction with domain examples. They do not retrain text recognition to repair recurring OCR character errors.
cards.misconception: Correcting field labels also repairs the underlying OCR recognizer.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

source.title: Validate document analyzer quality with confidence, grounding, and labeled samples
